c.adv.adv-01.headline: Apply 62 mm
c.adv.adv-01.learned: based on three seasons on this farm
c.adv.adv-01.reason: Soil moisture is low and 44 °C is forecast Tuesday
c.adv.adv-02.assumptions: Standard boom sprayer · 400 L water · 3 bar pressure
c.adv.adv-02.headline: Do not spray Tuesday
c.adv.adv-02.reason: High wind speed will reduce spray efficacy and cause drift beyond target area
c.adv.adv-03.action: Spray Dubas bug nymphs on fronds
c.adv.adv-03.assumptions: Drip irrigation not operating during spray
c.adv.adv-03.headline: Spray Dubas bug
c.adv.adv-03.ident: Dubas bug (Ommatissus lybicus) — small hemipteran, 3–4 mm, yellow nymphs with dark spots clustered on frond undersides, adults pale brown with red eyes
c.adv.adv-03.rate: 0.05 L/ha in 32 L water per hectare
c.adv.adv-03.reason: Dubas bug nymphs detected on 15% of fronds; population doubling every 3 days at current temperature
c.adv.adv-03.symptom.0: Yellow speckling on underside of leaflets
c.adv.adv-03.symptom.1: Honeydew sooty mould on fronds and ground below
c.adv.adv-03.symptom.2: Wilting and early senescence of fronds
c.adv.adv-04.headline: Apply 40 mm
c.adv.adv-04.reason: Soil moisture at 62% of available capacity; citrus ET is high at this temperature
c.adv.adv-05.assumptions: Granular application in furrow with irrigation
c.adv.adv-05.headline: Apply K₂SO₄
c.adv.adv-05.reason: Tissue potassium 1.8% dry matter — below 2.0% optimum for high-yield alfalfa
c.adv.adv-06.assumptions: Foliar spray at dawn to avoid sun scorch
c.adv.adv-06.headline: Foliar N and Zn
c.adv.adv-06.reason: Leaf tissue nitrogen 2.1% and zinc 18 mg/kg — both trending low; nitrogen supports fruit set
c.adv.adv-07.headline: Watch for dubas bug
c.adv.adv-07.reason: Conditions favour dubas bug (80%+ RH, 35–40 °C) from now to 7 Aug; early detection prevents explosion
c.adv.adv-08.assumptions: Hand harvest · early morning · cooling immediately
c.adv.adv-08.headline: Begin harvest P-03
c.adv.adv-08.learned: based on ripeness data from previous two seasons
c.adv.adv-08.reason: Sugar content 18 Brix reached; slight colour shift observed in 60% of bunches
c.adv.adv-09.assumptions: Scouting protocol: 15 leaves per tree, 10 trees per plot
c.adv.adv-09.headline: Scout for scale
c.adv.adv-09.reason: Scale insect pressure rising in hot season; adjacent plot (P-02) shows 8 per leaflet
c.adv.adv-10.headline: Monitor rain risk
c.adv.adv-10.reason: Unexpected rain during wheat flowering could reduce yield; alfalfa disease risk increases with leaf wetness
c.adv.adv-10.why.1.v: critical stage — rain = fungal disease risk
c.adv.adv-11.headline: Prune dead fronds
c.adv.adv-11.reason: Dead and brown fronds accumulate debris and reduce airflow; remove before next intensive monitoring cycle in September
c.adv.adv-11.why.3.v: pest scouting 20% faster with clear canopy
c.adv.adv-12.headline: Soil profiling
c.adv.adv-12.reason: New orchard requires soil profile calibration; no prior moisture data for model tuning
c.adv.adv-13.headline: Tissue N retest
c.adv.adv-13.reason: Last test 2 weeks ago showed 2.2% N; retest needed to confirm trend before applying corrective dose
c.adv.adv-14.assumptions: Apply at dusk to avoid heat stress
c.adv.adv-14.headline: Spray leaf miner
c.adv.adv-14.ident: Citrus leaf miner (Phyllocnistis citrella) — minute moth (4–6 mm), larva creates winding transparent mines in young leaves, pupates at mine end
c.adv.adv-14.rate: 0.18 L/ha in 18 L water per hectare
c.adv.adv-14.reason: Leaf miner mines visible in 22% of young shoots; early treatment prevents tunnel damage and defoliation
c.adv.adv-14.symptom.0: Transparent winding mines in new leaves
